paragraphs: Friend, here's what I love about this passage. Israel cried out to the LORD, and He answered, even though the prophet said they "did not obey" Him (Judges 6:10). Nobody earned this. God showed up first, and He showed up in a winepress, where a scared man was hiding his wheat. That's the kind of God we're baking for.

Now look at what the angel of the LORD says to Gideon: "The LORD is with you, O mighty man of valor" (Judges 6:12). Gideon isn't acting mighty. He says his clan is the weakest and that he's the youngest in his father's house (Judges 6:15). But the LORD doesn't argue about Gideon's résumé. He says, "Surely I will be with you" (Judges 6:16). The strength was never going to come from Gideon, baker. It comes from the One who is sending him.

Then the LORD gives Gideon a job close to home. Before any Midianite gets touched, Gideon has to tear down the altar to Baal in his own father's yard (Judges 6:25). He's afraid, so he does it by night, and he still does it (Judges 6:27). I think that's the part for us. You don't have to be fearless to obey, you just have to go. And the God who says "Do not be afraid" (Judges 6:23) walks right into the morning with you. This story isn't over, friend, and neither is yours.
